_note:
Marker is the Hello Panda packet, centred on the tray, LANDSCAPE orientation. Third marker attempt for this tray: the adaptor was near-uniform white (nothing for ARKit to match) and the tea packet was only 6.5cm (too small to detect at standing distance). This one is 14.3cm declared — larger than DR-11's Panadol box, which detects reliably — with dense high-contrast asymmetric print.

Geometry from IMG_8777, scaled off the packet's directly measured 13.2 x 8.8 cm. Worth recording why that matters: scaling instead off the previously-derived tray size gave 14.4 x 9.6 cm for the packet, i.e. every distance 8.9% too large, because that chain traced back to the tea packet's 6.5cm. The error was a clean uniform scale (both axes off by the same 1.089) rather than a misread outline, which is what identified it as a scale problem and not a geometry one. Measure the marker directly; don't derive it.

The crop is axis-aligned to the TRAY, not to the packet — the packet sits about 6 degrees off square, and cropping to the tray's axes means the marker's own frame already matches the tray's, so trayYawInMarkerSpaceDegrees stays 0 with no trigonometric compensation to get the sign wrong on. The white tray visible at the crop's corners is intentional and is genuinely part of what the camera sees.
